name: YC (TurnMeUpYC)
notes: The most-credited producer of the 2020–21 Memphis chart run. One parameter here is doing real work and it is a **mix decision expressed as register**: the research says the ostinato is thin and high and that the mix leaves the mid-range empty for a low male voice, so `melody.register` runs 72–94 — the highest lead in this batch by more than an octave — over a `bright_bell` timbre at 2–5 notes a bar. Everything below it follows: a hard 808 kick with layered attack, clap+snare on 3, triplet hats at 0.42 in a dry close mix (`quantizeStrength` 0.95), cowbell nearly off, and a tuned 808 with short glides and *medium* decay specifically so the hat pattern stays legible — `glideProb` 0.12, `followRootsProb` 0.9. The harmony is a single-chord i under a 2-bar motif, held by `impliedByRiff` and `chordDurationBeats` rather than by authored progressions; the research also names a sampled 4-bar progression when he works with the flip crew, and that reading is carried by the parent's multi-chord Memphis families, which this model inherits rather than replaces. ⛔ `low` because the research rates it medium-low and is unusually blunt about it: the credits and chart facts are sourced and **every sonic parameter here — tempo, kick, hats, velocities, the 808 decay — is a modern-Memphis lane inference**. ⚠ The countermelody sits at the engine's floor (0.3, two styles); the research says there is none. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 956 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 966/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [2,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 968/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.24 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 968/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
